name: Arizona
source: Arizona Department of Revenue Form 140 (2025) read on 2026-10-22 (taxsim.nber.org copy of FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2025_140_f.pdf): 2.5% of taxable income (line 46), 2,100 per person 65 or older (line 38), Social Security subtracted (line 30), 25% of long-term gains subtracted (line 24), government pensions up to 2,500 (line 29a); ADOR filing-threshold page (15,750 / 31,500 for 2025, the federal standard deduction); Tax Foundation 2026 state income tax table as second source

state_base.note: Arizona starts from federal adjusted (or taxable) income and keeps the federal treatment of 401(k) deferrals, Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits (no add-back; only California and New Jersey tax HSA deposits). Not checked against a state ruling.

standard_deduction.note: Arizona's standard deduction matches the federal amount (ADOR: 15,750 single and 31,500 joint for 2025, primary). 2026 uses the federal 16,100 / 32,200 on the June 2026 budget's full conformity (confirmed primary: https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01041.htm, validation run 2, 2026-10-22); Tax Foundation on 2026-01-01 still showed the pre-conformity 8,350 / 16,700. Not modelled: the 34% charitable increase.

exemptions.note: 2,100 exemption per taxpayer or spouse 65 or older (Form 140 line 38, primary). Dependents get the dependent tax credit instead (exemption_credits). Not modelled: the subtraction of the federal enhanced senior deduction (6,000 per person 65 or older, phased out above a modified AGI of 75,000 / 150,000, 2025 to 2028) that HB 4168 adds to ARS 43-1022(35) (https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57leg/2R/bills/HB4168H.htm, validation run 3, 2026-10-22); the file has no phase-out or end year for an exemption (law-backlog).

exemption_credits.note: Dependent tax credit: 125 per dependent under 17 for tax year 2026 (HB 4168, enacted fact sheet provision 9, https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57leg/2R/summary/S.4168-1861ATT_ASENACTED.DOCX.htm, confirmed primary, validation run 2, 2026-10-22); 25 for older dependents (not modelled); phased out above federal AGI 200,000 single / 400,000 joint (not modelled).

capital_gains_exclusion.note: 25% of net long-term capital gains from assets bought after 2011 is subtracted (Form 140 lines 23-24, primary); the model assumes every gain qualifies.

estate_inheritance.check_at: https://azdor.gov (Arizona repealed its estate tax in 2006)
estate_inheritance.note: Arizona has no estate tax and no inheritance tax (Tax Foundation 2026 estate and inheritance tax map, https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/estate-inheritance-taxes/, and state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax agree).

social_security.note: Arizona does not tax Social Security benefits; it is not among the states that tax them in Kiplinger 2026 (https://www.kiplinger.com/taxes/states-that-tax-social-security-benefits) and state-costs.csv column ss_taxed. Form 140 line 30 subtracts the federally taxed benefits (read 2026-10-22). Only government pensions (up to 2,500 per taxpayer, line 29a) and military pay have exclusions; IRA and private pension income is taxed in full, so no retirement_exclusion section.

local_income_tax.check_at: Tax Foundation local income taxes primer
local_income_tax.note: Arizona cities and counties levy no income tax (Tax Foundation local income tax list and state-costs.csv local_income_tax agree).

sales_tax.check_at: Arizona revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://azdor.gov/business/transaction-privilege-tax/model-city-tax-code/rate-and-code-updates and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: partly); research note: State TPT exempts food for home consumption; some cities tax it (ADOR Table 2 food column); local avg overstates. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Some towns tax groceries and others do not; the estimate uses the general average local rate, so it overstates. Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Confirmed primary on the Census ACS 2024 1-year tables (https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/latest?table_ids=B25090,B25082&geo_ids=04000US04, validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.note: Arizona vehicle license tax (A.R.S. 28-5801 to 5808): 2.80 per 100 of 60% of the list price in the first year and 2.89 after, the assessed value falling 16.25% a year; on a 29,100 car that is 489 in the first year and about 256 a year averaged over ten years. Small registration fees are left out. Typical car (29,100 list price, 2026 Toyota Camry LE), averaged over about ten years of ownership; registration and vehicle taxes only (no title, plate or inspection fees). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

fuel.source: Excise: USGasGauge/EIA (https://usgasgauge.com/gas-tax) and Kiplinger 2026 for some states, memory for the rest; price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Gas excise confirmed primary: 0.18 excise plus a 0.01 underground storage tank fee (https://www.azleg.gov/ars/49/01031.htm, validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand in validation run 3, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Arizona insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
